references.text: Repeats the prohibition against stealing as part of the holiness law in Leviticus.
Moses repeats the Ten Commandments, including the prohibition against stealing, in his farewell address to Israel.
The prophet Hosea accuses Israel of breaking the commandments, including theft.
Jeremiah rebukes the people for stealing and then coming to the temple and feeling secure.
Jesus quotes the command 'You shall not steal' when he answers the rich young man about how he can inherit eternal life.
Paul quotes the command against stealing as part of love fulfilling the law.
Paul urges that whoever stole must no longer steal, but instead work and share with others.
Jesus mentions the command against stealing in his conversation with the rich man.
Jesus quotes the commandments, including the prohibition against stealing, to the rich ruler.
Paul asks rhetorically whether the one who teaches others not to steal steals himself.
